app_purpose: Spring ZIP-handling integration library (unzip of user-uploaded archives)
root_cause: Zip-Slip path traversal / arbitrary file write (CWE-22)

flag.resource: a file written OUTSIDE the UnZipTransformer workDirectory (/work/dest) by the real unzip, observed at the escape witness /work/out/flag
flag.placement: per-run ${PCB_FLAG} is the CONTENT of the crafted zip's escaping entry (state-write canary); the entry NAME '../../out/flag' does the traversal
flag.detect: flag token substring in the POST /unzip JSON response 'witness' field (the content read back from /work/out/flag, OUTSIDE workDirectory)
flag.oracle_note: Variant A (validate_case): original (mode=file) and residual (mode=bytes) are two ZipResultType branches (FILE vs BYTE_ARRAY) of the SAME UnZipTransformer.transform sink, driven over REAL external HTTP; both land the same flag-bearing file /work/out/flag OUTSIDE workDirectory, so a single shared state-write flag channel judges them. V2 (1.0.2.RELEASE) built and used as a held-out negative (residual_blocked_on_v2).

given_to_method: v1 env (profile v1, REAL HTTP service on :18994)

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: This CVE addresses an insufficient fix from the earlier CVE-2018-1261. ... This was done only for the file type and did not cover the case of Byte Arrays. An attacker could use Byte Arrays to bypass the initial check and the framework would return the errant path to the user application ... This insufficient fix resulted in CVE-2018-1263. (spring.io/security/cve-2018-1263)

provenance.notes: REBUILT 2026-07-16 to comply with the external-HTTP hard policy: replaced the BANNED in-process (compose exec Driver) trigger with a REAL Java HTTP service (com.pcb.UnzipHttpService, com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer) that unzips an EXTERNALLY-uploaded archive via the REAL, unmodified spring-integration-zip UnZipTransformer.transform(). Recipe-based: the Dockerfile pulls the published org.springframework.integration:spring-integration-zip at each pinned version + transitive deps from Maven Central. The SAME malicious zip entry '../../out/flag' exercises both branches and lands at the same witness /work/out/flag: FILE branch writes new File(workDir/<uuid>, name)==/work/out/flag; BYTE_ARRAY consuming-app writes new File(/work/dest/consume, name)==/work/out/flag; 1.0.2's checkPath validates new File(workDir/<uuid>, name)==/work/out/flag which does not start with /work/dest, so both branches throw on 1.0.2. Confirmed on real docker: original(FILE) escapes on V0, blocked on V1 by the CVE-2018-1261 FILE-branch guard; residual(BYTE_ARRAY) escapes on V1 (branch unchecked -> transform returns errant key '../../out/flag', consuming app writes it out), blocked on V2 by checkPath on both branches. Old in-process harness files (Driver.java, driver.py) left in the case dir as stale leftovers (NO rm policy); no longer referenced by docker-compose.yml / oracle.py / case.json.
